messages:
Sam A.: hitting intermittent SSL/502 errors for a couple of private/VPC customers after last night's rotator run. seeing `tls: handshake failure` and `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority` in edge logs. anyone on-call?
Anya (Support): we have two escalations. customers see SDK calls failing ~10-30% of requests, only from their private attachments. ticket IDs in case notes.
Sam A.: pasted a quick debug from one affected host: 
```
$ openssl s_client -connect private-api.internal:443 -servername private-api.internal -showcerts
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=0 CN = private-api.internal
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
verify return:0
---
Certificate chain
0 s:/CN=private-api.internal
   i:/CN=Example Intermediate CA
---
```
chain only shows leaf + (what looks like) intermediate, but clients report the intermediate is not being accepted. curl -v returns `SSL: no alternative certificate` intermittently.
rotator-bot: rotation completed 2025-11-01T03:12:00Z, bundle id `rb-20251101-0312`, artifact s3://rotator/bundles/rb-20251101-0312.pem, previous bundle `rb-20251031-2301` retained.
Mike Ops: logs from the rotator job show the bundle concatenation step ran like: `cat $ROOT $INTERMEDIATE > $BUNDLE` — that's suspicious. If root is concatenated before intermediate, many TLS stacks will reject the chain. we've seen this before.
Lee - Infra: can we confirm whether frontend proxies (envoy/haproxy) were reloaded with the new bundle or if they're pulling from a cache? Envoy caches certs on hot-restart unless told to re-read. also double-check OCSP stapling behavior.
Sam A.: customer tcpdump showed repeated OCSP timeouts and `staple: no response` from the proxy. example snippet from their capture: `TLSv1.3 (IN), CertificateVerify, length 256` then `alert (fatal): handshake_failure`.
Anya (Support): customer also mentions these started right after the maintenance window when the rotator job ran and firewall changes were applied last week to tighten egress. could be two issues compounding.
Mike Ops: traced egress from our rotator/edge workers to the CA's OCSP responder: `telnet ocsp.example-ca.com 80` times out from the private network. firewall rule `egress-block-v3` denies outbound to 0.0.0.0/0 except whitelisted — we probably never whitelisted the OCSP host for that VPC pool.
Lee - Infra: proposed action items:
1) Roll back to previous bundle `rb-20251031-2301` on affected private clusters (mitigation) — assigned to me (Lee).
2) Restart envoy/haproxy on affected nodes to force chain reload (Lee).
3) Patch rotator concatenation ordering logic to ensure `leaf -> intermediate(s) -> root` (Mike Ops + rotator owner).
4) Add explicit egress allowlist entry for known OCSP/CRL endpoints used by our CA providers (network).
5) Add post-rotation smoke check that runs `openssl s_client -connect <host>:443 -verify_return_error -showcerts` and validates chain and stapling (Sam).
Sam A.: repro steps for support/SE to validate a host after mitigation: 
```
# check chain and stapling
openssl s_client -connect private-api.internal:443 -servername private-api.internal -showcerts
# verify OCSP stapling status
openssl s_client -connect private-api.internal:443 -status -servername private-api.internal
```
Mike Ops: rolled back bundle on clusters pvt-usa-1 and pvt-eu-2 at 2025-11-01T15:23:00Z, restarted envoys. Metrics show failed calls dropped from ~12/min to <1/min within 6 minutes.
Anya (Support): customers reported dramatically fewer errors after the rollback. I'm sending an update and marking the escalations as mitigated for now — will keep them in watch for 24h.
Mike Ops: root cause summary for postmortem: rotator concatenated certs in incorrect order which produced an invalid chain for some client stacks, and at the same time egress allowlists blocked OCSP responders causing stapling/timeouts — combined effect produced intermittent handshake failures for private VPC customers. fix plans: rotator hotfix (unit + integration tests), network allowlist update, post-rotation smoke tests, and an incident blameless postmortem.
Lee - Infra: taking ownership of the rollback and egress rule change. Mike will own rotator fix. Sam will own the smoke test. Anya will keep customer comms.
Anya (Support): thanks team — I'll follow up with customers and close the tickets once we confirm 24h of stability. :thumbsup:
